newsitem.title: SUDAN: Sudan says inflicts casualties on Eritrea troops.
newsitem.headline: Sudan says inflicts casualties on Eritrea troops.

text.p: A senior Sudanese official said in comments published on Monday that government forces had inflicted heavy casualties on Eritrean forces fighting alongside rebels in northeast Sudan.
The government-owned al-Sudan al-Hadith newspaper quoted Army Brigadier Mohammad Ali Abdalla, minister of social and cultural affairs, as saying Eritrean troops fell near the district of Aqiq.
The government has dismissed rebel claims to control Aqiq and accuses Eritrea and Ethiopia of sending troops to support rebels. Both countries deny the charge.
A coalition of forces under the command of Sudan People's Liberation Army (SPLA) leader John Garang is fighting to overthrow Khartoum's Islamist government.

Garang said in a statement issued in the Eritrean capital Asmara on Tuesday that rebels had seized several northeastern districts in an offensive to cut the road between Khartoum and Sudan's main link to the outside world at Port Sudan on the Red Sea.
But Abdalla said: "Our armed forces have been able to inflict on the Eritrean enemy huge losses in lives and equipment south of Aqiq town."
A Sudanese member of parliament said Eritrea was waging psychological war against Sudan by moving troops into the areas of Karora and Itairaba.

Musa Hussein Dirar, head of the mobilisation committee in the National Assembly, Sudan's parliament, told al-Sudan al-Hadith there were a large number of Eritrean soldiers in the area supported by 20 tanks.
Garang said last week the rebel coalition had "liberated" Karora and Itairaba along with Aqiq and Agiti and were advancing on the town of Tokar, 150 km (90 miles) southeast of Port Sudan.

"After touring the frontline, I found our forces had faced the build-up with steadfastness and bravery," Dirar said. He said Eritrean and Ethiopian forces were doing most of the fighting and there were few rebel forces.
